title: Momentum Module 1 Lesson 1: Momentum Conservation Direct Collision custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A particle $P$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ travels along a straight horizontal track with a speed of $4.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the magnitude of the linear momentum of $P$.

Taking motion to the right as positive, particle $A$ has mass $1.2\text{ kg}$ moving right at $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and particle $B$ has mass $0.8\text{ kg}$ moving left at $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the total initial linear momentum of the system.

A particle $P$ of mass $2\text{ kg}$ moving at $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides directly with a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$. After the collision, $P$ continues in its original direction with speed $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the speed of $Q$ after the collision.

Two particles $A$ (mass $0.5\text{ kg}$) and $B$ (mass $0.4\text{ kg}$) move towards each other with speeds $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ respectively. After collision, particle $A$ rebounds with speed $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the speed and direction of motion of $B$ after the collision.

A particle $X$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$ moving at $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides directly with a stationary particle $Y$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$. After impact, $X$ continues in the same direction at $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $Y$ moves forward at $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the mass $m$ of particle $X$.

A sphere of mass $0.75\text{ kg}$ travelling at speed $u\text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides directly with a stationary sphere of mass $1.25\text{ kg}$. The collision brings the first sphere instantaneously to rest, and the second sphere moves off with speed $2.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate $u$.

questions.prompt: Two small smooth spheres $A$ and $B$, of masses $0.4\text{ kg}$ and $0.6\text{ kg}$ respectively, move in the same direction along a straight horizontal line on a smooth horizontal floor. Sphere $A$ has speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and sphere $B$ has speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Sphere $A$ collides directly with sphere $B$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that immediately after the collision sphere $A$ continues to move in its original direction with speed $2.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$, find the speed of sphere $B$ immediately after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the change in the momentum of sphere $A$ resulting from the collision, stating its magnitude and direction.

questions.prompt: Two particles $P$ and $Q$ have masses $0.8\text{ kg}$ and $0.5\text{ kg}$ respectively. They move towards each other on a smooth horizontal plane with speeds $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ respectively, and collide directly.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: In the collision, particle $P$ is brought to instantaneous rest. Find the speed and direction of motion of particle $Q$ immediately after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total loss of kinetic energy of the system caused by the collision.

questions.prompt: Two particles $A$ and $B$, of masses $m\text{ kg}$ and $0.45\text{ kg}$ respectively, are moving towards each other in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface with speeds $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ respectively. The particles collide directly. Immediately after the collision, the speed of $A$ is $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and the speed of $B$ is $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that particle $A$ continues to move in its original direction after the collision, find the mass $m$ of particle $A$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Suppose instead that the direction of motion of $A$ is reversed by the collision. Show that this scenario is mathematically impossible given that the floor is smooth and $m > 0$.

questions.prompt: A trolley $X$ of mass $1.5\text{ kg}$ moves with constant speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a straight horizontal rail. It collides directly with a stationary trolley $Y$ of mass $2.5\text{ kg}$. In the collision, trolley $X$ is not brought to rest.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that the speed of trolley $Y$ immediately after the collision is $4.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, find the speed and direction of motion of trolley $X$ immediately after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: After the collision, trolley $Y$ enters a rough horizontal section of the rail where the coefficient of friction between the trolley and the rail is $0.35$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the distance trolley $Y$ travels along the rough rail before coming to rest.

questions.prompt: A block $B$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$ is sliding across a smooth horizontal table with speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. A small ball $A$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ falls vertically from rest from a height of $1.8\text{ m}$ above the block. The ball strikes the block and the horizontal component of the ball's velocity immediately before impact is zero.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the vertical speed with which the ball strikes the block.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: During the impact, the ball rebounds vertically upwards with speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, while a brief horizontal friction force between the ball and the block gives the ball a horizontal speed of $1.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in the direction of motion of the block. Find the speed of the block immediately after the impact, and the impulse exerted on the block in the horizontal direction.

questions.prompt: Three identical small smooth spheres $A$, $B$, and $C$, each of mass $m\text{ kg}$, lie in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface with $B$ between $A$ and $C$. Initially, $B$ and $C$ are at rest and $A$ moves towards $B$ with speed $u\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Sphere $A$ collides directly with sphere $B$. Immediately after this first collision, $A$ moves in its original direction with speed $\frac{1}{4}u$. Sphere $B$ subsequently collides directly with sphere $C$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the speed of sphere $B$ immediately after the first collision with sphere $A$ is $\frac{3}{4}u$, and find the impulse exerted by sphere $A$ on sphere $B$ in terms of $m$ and $u$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: In the second collision, sphere $B$ collides directly with sphere $C$. Immediately after this collision, sphere $C$ moves with speed $V\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and sphere $B$ continues to move in the same direction with speed $w\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Given that there is no subsequent collision between sphere $A$ and sphere $B$, find the inequality that $w$ must satisfy, and determine the corresponding range of possible values of $V$ in terms of $u$.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at the top of a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The length of the inclined plane is $2.5\text{ m}$. At the bottom of the incline, $P$ transitions smoothly onto a smooth horizontal floor without loss of speed. It then travels across the horizontal floor and collides directly with a particle $Q$ of mass $1.5\text{ kg}$ which is moving towards $P$ with speed $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the speed of particle $P$ as it reaches the horizontal floor is $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: In the collision on the horizontal floor, particle $P$ rebounds and moves back towards the incline with speed $1.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the speed of particle $Q$ immediately after the collision, and determine whether particle $P$ will reach the top of the inclined plane on its rebound.
